speaker: President David A. Bednar
text: Ah, {player}, there you are. Come in, please.

speaker: President David A. Bednar
text: This college is about to grow in ways most people can’t imagine yet, and I’m going to need your help.

speaker: President David A. Bednar
text: {player}, look at what we’ve done together. Teachers hired, buildings raised, and a new name on the sign.

speaker: President David A. Bednar
text: Go and see the campus as it is today. I think you’ll be proud of what it became.

speaker: President Bednar
text: Thank you for coming. Our college is growing, and our students will need more great teachers.

speaker: President Bednar
text: Four faculty candidates are waiting in Personnel Services, just down the hall: math, English, art and engineering.

speaker: President Bednar
text: Walk each one to their department for a teaching demonstration. The art studio's projector has been acting up, so start with art before engineering. Then come back and report to me.

speaker: President Bednar
text: Math, English, art and engineering — and I hear the Spori's projector works again.

speaker: President Bednar
text: These teachers will bless many students. Well done.

speaker: President Bednar
text: {player}, it’s good to see you. The years have flown by, haven’t they? Look how much this campus has grown.

speaker: President Bednar
text: I have one more job for you. Four letters are hidden around campus, right in plain sight. These cards will help you find them.

speaker: President Bednar
text: Once you have them, bring them to the sign by the roundabout. Let’s finish it together.

speaker: President Bednar
text: All four are hired? Wonderful — tell me about them.

speaker: President Bednar
text: Keep those cards handy, {player}. Check your journal whenever you need a clue, and bring each letter to the sign by the roundabout.

speaker: Sister Ames
text: Hi! I'm due in the Romney Building to teach the computer science students. They're stuck on binary — I have an idea from Alma 11.

speaker: Sister Ames
text: I tried this lesson on my little brother. He's eight. He got it in five minutes.

speaker: Sister Ames
text: Fun fact: a limnah is exactly a shum, a seon and a senine. That's my whole hook.

speaker: Sister Ames
text: Over here! Ready when you are.

speaker: Department chair
text: Class, this is our math candidate. Our computer science students keep tripping on binary. Sister Ames, could you explain it so it finally sticks?

speaker: Department chair
text: That's the clearest binary lesson I've seen. I'll recommend you to President Bednar.

speaker: Department chair
text: Thank you! I think it finally clicked for them.

speaker: Brother Nielsen
text: Hello. My demonstration is in the Smith Building — a student's write-up needs a careful red pen.

speaker: Brother Nielsen
text: Brother Price wrote the summary himself. I hope he doesn't mind a little red ink.

speaker: Brother Nielsen
text: Rule one of editing: check the facts against a source. Rule two: be kind about it.

speaker: Brother Nielsen
text: There you are! Shall we head in?

speaker: Department chair
text: Class, this is our English candidate. Brother Price has volunteered his write-up of the Kimball Building dedication. Brother Nielsen, would you show us how to edit it for accuracy?

speaker: Department chair
text: Careful, kind and accurate. I'll recommend you to President Bednar.

speaker: Department chair
text: Thank you — and thanks, Brother Price, for being a good sport.

speaker: Sister Okada
text: Hi there! My demo is up in the old Spori's art studio. I'll be teaching the grid method.

speaker: Sister Okada
text: I just hope that old projector in the Spori survives the demo.

speaker: Sister Okada
text: The grid method is simple: one square at a time, and don't panic.

speaker: Sister Okada
text: Hi! The studio's on the third floor.

speaker: Department chair
text: Class, meet our art candidate. Our students struggle to draw what they actually see. Sister Okada, can you show them how? If that old projector cooperates.

speaker: Department chair
text: Even with the projector dying, you kept the class drawing. I'll recommend you to President Bednar.

speaker: Department chair
text: Thank you! Someone should look at that projector, though.

speaker: Brother Ruiz
text: Ready when you are. I'm demonstrating in the Austin Building's electronics lab.

speaker: Brother Ruiz
text: I'm waiting on the art department's demo first — I hear their old projector is about to short out — that's what I'll be fixing.

speaker: Brother Ruiz
text: I heard the Spori's projector died in the middle of the art demo. Perfect timing, honestly.

speaker: Brother Ruiz
text: A short circuit is just electricity taking the lazy way home. Let's fix that.

speaker: Brother Ruiz
text: Did the art demo finish? Let's go fix that projector.

speaker: Department chair
text: Class, this is our engineering candidate. Physical Plant just brought us the Spori's projector; it shorted out during the art demo. Brother Ruiz, can you fix it and explain what went wrong?

speaker: Department chair
text: Fixed it live, and they understood why. I'll recommend you to President Bednar.

speaker: Department chair
text: Thank you! Tell the art studio their projector is ready.

speaker: Sister Ames
text: I'm not ready yet.

speaker: Sister Ames
text: The other candidates will meet you outside their buildings — they're marked on your map.

speaker: Student
text: I’ve got a chemistry test in the Romney Building in ten minutes. Pray for me.

speaker: Student
text: The Manwaring Center has the best snacks on campus. Don’t tell anyone.

speaker: Student
text: Go Vikings! Are you coming to the game at the stadium?

speaker: Student
text: Rexburg winters are no joke. Bring a real coat, not a fashion coat.

speaker: Student
text: I’m headed to the library to study. It’s the quietest place on campus.

speaker: Student
text: Everyone keeps joking that the computers will break when it turns 2000.

speaker: Student
text: The new Kimball Building looks amazing. I heard the president’s office is in there.

speaker: Student
text: Watch out for the golf carts. They come around corners fast.

speaker: Student
text: I keep finding coins on the sidewalks. Free money!

speaker: Student
text: Intramurals on the upper fields tonight. You in?

speaker: Student
text: Have you seen the old Spori Building? It’s been here forever.

speaker: Student
text: My roommate auditioned at the Snow Building. She was so nervous.

speaker: Student
text: I took a photo by the pond near the Manwaring Center. So pretty in the fall.

speaker: Student
text: There’s a devotional this week. Want to sit together?

speaker: Student
text: I’m from out of state. Idaho is way flatter than I expected… except this hill.

speaker: Student
text: The Hart gym is packed every night. Good luck finding a court.

speaker: Student
text: Professors here actually learn your name. That’s the best part.

speaker: Student
text: I signed up for a ballroom class. Two left feet, but I’m trying.

speaker: Student
text: Did you see? The old Spori Building is gone. They’re planning something new.

speaker: Student
text: There are construction fences everywhere. Something big is coming.

speaker: Student
text: I heard there’s a brand-new building going up near the Taylor Building.

speaker: Student
text: Things feel different on campus this year. Exciting different.

speaker: Student
text: The Hart gym is still packed every night.

speaker: Student
text: I can’t wait to see what they build next.

speaker: Student
text: Free hot chocolate at the Manwaring Center today!

speaker: Student
text: My professor says the campus is growing faster than ever.

speaker: Student
text: The pond by the Manwaring Center freezes in winter. Don’t walk on it!

speaker: Student
text: Have you been inside the big new Center? It holds thousands of people.

speaker: Student
text: The temple on the hill looks beautiful at night.

speaker: Student
text: I heard someone hid letters all over campus. Weird, right?

speaker: Student
text: The sign by the roundabout looks unfinished. I wonder why.

speaker: Student
text: The library is my second home during finals.

speaker: Student
text: The Snow Building has a concert every weekend.

speaker: Student
text: I love walking past the Hart Building when the teams are training.

speaker: Student
text: Campus keeps getting bigger every year.

speaker: Student
text: Did you know the pond by the Manwaring Center has lily pads?

speaker: Student
text: Welcome to BYU–Idaho!

speaker: Student
text: Big devotional in the I-Center this week.

speaker: Student
text: The STC is where all the science happens.

speaker: Student
text: Can you believe this all used to be Ricks College?

speaker: Student
text: Heading to the upper fields for intramurals!

speaker: Student
text: I heard there’s a hackathon celebration in the STC today!

speaker: Student
text: The temple grounds are so peaceful.

speaker: Student
text: The I-Center track is great when it’s snowing outside.

speaker: Student
text: Coins on the sidewalk again? This campus is lucky.

speaker: Student
text: I love the new sign by the roundabout.
